messages:
Olga Petrov: quick q for anyone tracking RBAC v2 — how do I grant *read-only auditor* access for an internal audit? I need someone to view org settings + deployment config + audit logs without being able to change anything.

Daniel Carter: +1, also need something we can point auditors at (role template name / link). right now i'm hand-holding with temp admin and i hate it.

Marcus Lin: yep, we have a draft built-in role template for this. it’s called `Read-only Auditor` (template key in policy bundle is currently `auditor_read_only`). it’s intended to be deny-by-default + explicit read perms.
Marcus Lin: internal doc is here (still WIP): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SEC/RBAC+v2+Role+Templates+and+Matrix
Marcus Lin: and the draft spreadsheet view (same content): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/security-and-compliance/rbac-v2-role-matrix-spreadsheet (look for “Auditor (Read-only)”).

Naomi Feldman: adding: we’re trying to standardize “Auditor can *view* audit logs, but *export* is separate” bc export to SIEM is a higher-risk data movement action. so check what you actually need.

Olga Petrov: they mostly need to verify controls + look at audit trail. export isn’t required but would be nice.

Fiona McCarthy: pls keep export separate unless we have a real requirement. if they need export, we should do a timeboxed elevated role + monitor.

Chloe Martin: current state (as of this week): Console UI for role assignment is behind the dogfood flag, so fastest path is API/cli.
Chloe Martin: if you have `rwctl`, this is the pattern we’ve been using in dogfood:
```bash
# 1) find org_id
rwctl orgs get --slug <org-slug>

# 2) create role binding (org scope) for a user
rwctl rbac role-bindings create \
  --org <org_id> \
  --scope org:<org_id> \
  --role-template auditor_read_only \
  --subject user:<email>

# OR bind an IdP group (preferred)
rwctl rbac role-bindings create \
  --org <org_id> \
  --scope org:<org_id> \
  --role-template auditor_read_only \
  --subject group:<idp-group-name>
```
Chloe Martin: if you don’t have rwctl access, the equivalent is the Control Plane endpoint `POST /v2/orgs/{org_id}/rbac/role_bindings` with subject + template.

David Kim: +1 on group mapping. for internal audits we usually create an Okta group like `audit-redwood-<org>-ro` and bind that. helps with offboarding.
David Kim: if you go the user-binding route, please set a calendar reminder to remove it, or ping IT.

Felix Schneider: note: in Console (when enabled) it’s under Org Settings → Access → Role bindings → “Assign role” → pick template “Read-only Auditor”. there’s also a permission viewer/search but it’s not in prod yet.
Felix Schneider: we’re also adding a “why was I denied?” drawer w/ denial reason codes, but again — still behind flag.

Daniel Carter: what permissions does the auditor role actually include right now?

Marcus Lin: rough summary (subject to final catalog):
- ✅ read org metadata, projects, environments
- ✅ read model/policy config (incl routing policy *view*)
- ✅ read deployment status and logs (view only)
- ✅ read audit log *entries* + filters
- ❌ no key mgmt (create/rotate/revoke)
- ❌ no user/role changes
- ❌ no policy edits
- ❌ no audit export (separate perm)
Marcus Lin: if you specifically need audit export, we have a second template draft called `auditor_export` but Security wants it gated + time-bound. (not a built-in “default” role)

Olga Petrov: makes sense. for this one, read-only is fine.

Connor O'Brien: heads up: if you’re doing this for a customer-facing org (vs internal-only), check whether their deployment is on Hosted vs Dedicated/Private. scope semantics are the same, but some older Dedicated tenants are still in “RBAC v1 compat” mode and the binding won’t take effect unless the `rbac_v2_eval` flag is on.
Connor O'Brien: if you hit a case where auditor still gets 403s, ping #eng-platform with org_id and we’ll confirm their flag status.

Naomi Feldman: also: when you assign, choose org scope unless you *only* want them to view one project. auditors usually need org-wide for evidence.

Olga Petrov: great, thank you all. i’ll do an Okta group + org-scope role binding and skip export.

Fiona McCarthy: if anyone asks for “just for an hour” admin instead, use break-glass. don’t stack random perms on top. :please:

Daniel Carter: thanks — I’ll reference the confluence role template doc in the evidence package (and the binding record).
